mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate authorization resolution and board minutes approving the ULC incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder or holding entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated bank or prime broker of the applicant

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, beneficial owners, and HFT trading counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations consolidated sanctions lists, the consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, plus FINTRAC guidance on domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs). Screening must be completed prior to incorporation, refreshed at least every 24 hours for trading counterparties, and documented for Canadian AML/CFT compliance under the PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Government of Alberta), accessible through authorized corporate registry service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in English or French, or a transliteration into the Latin alphabet using alphanumeric characters. For an Alberta unlimited liability corporation, the name must include one of the following prescribed legal elements: 'ULC', 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'SRI', or 'Société à responsabilité illimitée'. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must meet Alberta Business Corporations Act naming standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with the Registrar of Corporations within 30 days of the rejection notification. The objection must state the proposed name, rejection reference number, legal grounds, and any supporting evidence of existing trade mark or corporate name rights. Submissions are made through the Alberta Corporate Registry portal or by serving the Registrar at the designated registry address. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the registered office requirement provided a registered agent in Alberta accepts service of process; however, for proprietary algorithmic high-frequency trading, a nominal registered office alone will generally not satisfy exchange membership, FINTRAC AML compliance, or commercial substance expectations. A physical presence in Canada or in a recognized financial market center is advisable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-high (60%) for a registered trading entity due to FINTRAC supervision and exchange oversight; low (20%) if the ULC is a passive holding vehicle only.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, sections 10–15 (certificate of incorporation), 15.1–15.2 (unlimited liability corporation), and 102 (organizational meeting); Corporate Registry Regulation (AR 100/98); Income Tax Act (Canada), Part XVII.1 (SIFT regime inapplicable to a qualifying ULC).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation (with integrated Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors), accompanied by a valid NUANS Name Search Report, filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta ULC; nominal authorized share capital may be established with Class A voting common shares and Class B non-voting common shares issued at CAD 1.00 per share. No escrow account or mandatory capital deposit applies at formation; escrow obligations arise only in connection with future public distributions under securities legislation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for the Class A and Class B Common Shares of the Corporation, per the subscription register, is accepted; the board shall issue certificates upon payment of agreed consideration in accordance with the Articles. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at Suite 3500, 1888 4th Street SW, Calgary, Alberta, T2W 3J9, Canada. RESOLVED, that Jane Doe, Chief Executive Officer; John Smith, Chief Financial Officer; and Alex Chen, Corporate Secretary, are appointed, each authorized to open bank accounts, execute exchange participant agreements, and file all regulatory approvals necessary to commence proprietary algorithmic trading operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online portal (RegistryXpress) or an accredited NUANS service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request for the proposed corporate name, which must include the prescribed suffix 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Review the search report for identical or confusingly similar existing corporate names and trade marks, then reserve the cleared name for a 90-day validity period to support the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name complying with ABCA distinctiveness and ULC suffix rules
Completed NUANS name search request form
Payment of approximate CAD 40 name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report reveals a conflict, the applicant must either select a revised distinctive corporate name and file a new search, or obtain a written consent letter from the conflicting rights holder; search fees are non-refundable, but re-submission carries no administrative penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Submission of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (RegistryXpress electronic filing; counter service in Edmonton or Calgary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate name, registered office address, authorized share structure (including the unlimited liability election), restrictions on business or share transfers, and the first directors. Attach each director's signed consent to act, and file electronically with the prescribed fee. The Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors are integrated into the filing package.
required_dossiers: Signed and dated Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation
Valid NUANS Name Search Report (issued within 90 days)
Integrated Notice of Registered Office
Integrated Notice of Directors
Executed Consent to Act as Director for each first director
Payment of CAD 200 standard electronic filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice or correction query, the incorporator must respond via RegistryXpress within 30 calendar days, file amended articles or supplementary consents, and pay a correction fee of approximately CAD 30–60; expedited priority processing of 2 business days is available upon payment of the additional priority fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of the Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the Articles, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of the corporate existence of the ULC. The incorporator retrieves the certified electronic or paper copy, establishes the statutory minute book, prepares or adopts the by-laws, and issues initial share certificates to subscribing shareholders.
required_dossiers: Approved Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Registry payment receipt
Minute book formation records (internal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is not issued within the anticipated SLA, escalate to Service Alberta Corporate Registry client services for status verification; certified duplicate certificates may be obtained for a prescribed fee if the original is lost, damaged, or requires reissuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, Adoption of First Board Resolution, and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation acting under section 102 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the board to adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription acceptance, registered office confirmation, officer appointments, banking authorizations, corporate seal, and share certificate form. Record minutes in the minute book, approve the operational by-laws, and file Form 2 (Notice of Change of Directors) if the officer appointments differ from the filed director list.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution and minutes of the organizational meeting
Officer appointment and acceptance forms
Bank account mandate and specimen signature cards
Form 2 – Notice of Change of Directors (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointed officer or director is disqualified or declines the position, the board shall pass a corrective resolution, update the minute book, and file a revised Form 2 with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 15 days; no regulatory penalty applies for a timely correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration (CRA Business Number, GST/HST, and Alberta Corporate Tax Account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (ATRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated ULC with the CRA through the Business Registration Online portal or by filing Form RC1 to obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN); open the corporate income tax account and the GST/HST account where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. Register with ATRA for the Alberta corporate income tax account (8% provincial flat rate) and confirm whether any municipal business licence or home-office permit applies to the trading floor location.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Completed CRA Form RC1 – Request for a Business Number
Directors' and officers' government-issued identification
Canadiana registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or ATRA returns a query or rejects the registration, the applicant must correct the flagged information and re-submit via CRA My Business Account or in writing, attaching a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation; expedited business number issuance is available by contacting the CRA business registry by telephone.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Securities Commission (ASC), Capital Markets Regulation; Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO); TMX Group Limited Market Participant Administration for exchange access
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Restricted Dealer Registration under the Securities Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c S-4, together with Approved Participant status at the designated Canadian exchange and clearing membership for proprietary ultra-low-latency market making access

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category Office/Information Technology under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c E-12; no mandatory EIA report for a low-density, non-emitting trading-floor operation; voluntary site environmental registration is recommended for e-waste and server cooling-fluid management.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source process wastewater or VOC emissions from the trading infrastructure; compliance with municipal sanitary sewer bylaws for domestic effluent; server-room refrigerants governed by the Ozone-depleting Substances and Halocarbons Regulation (AR 124/94); electronic waste disposed exclusively through Alberta Recycling Management Authority approved collectors under the Electronic Waste Regulation (AR 447/2009).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Certificate issued by the local fire authority per the Alberta Fire Code adopted under the Safety Codes Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c S-1; electrical installation clearance for UPS systems and high-density server racks; structural load verification for raised computer floors; Occupational Health and Safety Code (2009) compliance covering emergency evacuation, first-aid provisions, ergonomic workstations, and business continuity planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portals: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO). Alberta corporate income tax is administered federally by the CRA under the Alberta Tax Collection Agreement (Alberta Corporate Tax Act, RSA 2000, c A-15); there is no separate Alberta corporate tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the unlimited liability company (ULC) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, s 15, filing articles that impose unlimited shareholder liability; obtain the Alberta Corporate Access Number. Step 2: Complete a single registration with the CRA via BRO (online), by phone at 1-800-959-5525, or by filing Form RC1, to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) which is the statutory TIN for federal Part I tax, Alberta corporate tax, and GST/HST; open program accounts for GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and import/export (RM) only if required. Step 3: Foreign-controlled ULCs must satisfy the ABCA Canadian-residency requirement for directors (at least 25% of the board, minimum one, must be resident Canadians). Step 4: Elect the fiscal year-end and file Form T2 within six months of year-end; a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Alberta with a permanent establishment there must file a T2 and may claim relief under the Canada-US Tax Convention.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (domestic Income Tax Act: an Alberta ULC is a resident corporation taxed on worldwide income under Part I, with provincial income allocated to Alberta at the 8% general rate). Pass_Through_Eligible solely for US-resident members under Article IV(6) of the Canada-US Tax Convention (fiscally transparent look-through entity) and under US check-the-box principles because shareholders bear unlimited liability; proprietary algorithm high-frequency trading income generally constitutes a specified investment business, precluding the small business deduction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (1) Canada-US Treaty Article IV(6) look-through election, implemented by notice of reliance appended to the ULC T2 return, with a supporting US Form 8832 entity classification election (the ULC is a foreign eligible entity with default partnership or disregarded-entity treatment for US purposes); (2) ETA s 156 election for closely related corporations to treat intercompany supplies of the HFT group as made for nil consideration for GST/HST; (3) selected listed financial institution special attribution method election under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, where the ULC is a listed financial institution; (4) no provincial check-the-box analog exists, and hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss 18.4, 18.5, 20.1) operate automatically without election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax, a federal value-added tax administered by the CRA; Alberta has no provincial sales tax or HST, so the effective rate is the 5% federal-GST-only regime). Trading in financial instruments and market-making services are generally exempt supplies under Schedule V, Part VII of the Excise Tax Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters of worldwide taxable supplies (ETA s 148 small-supplier threshold). Exempt financial supplies do not count toward the threshold; however, a listed financial institution, including a securities dealer whose principal business is trading in financial instruments such as an HFT market-making ULC, cannot be a small supplier and must account for GST/HST under the special attribution method for selected listed financial institutions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based e-invoicing regime exists in Canada; the CRA is progressively adopting the Pan-Canadian Peppol BIS 3.0 e-invoicing framework on a voluntary basis only. Tax invoices must contain the prescribed content under ETA s 169(1) (supplier name and BN, date, recipient identity, description, consideration, and GST rate). Registrants with annual taxable supplies of at least CAD 1,000,000 must file GST/HST returns electronically (NETFILE) and remit electronically where mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% rating under ETA Schedule VI, Part V where the supplier sells and physically exports the goods with delivery outside Canada within the prescribed time. Services: Schedule VI, Part V zero-rates services supplied to non-resident persons for consumption wholly outside Canada, excluding services relating to Canadian real property or personal services rendered in Canada; financial services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part VII. For proprietary HFT, principal trading gains and market-making spreads are exempt or outside the GST/HST net; execution rebates and platform fees are zero-rated only when supplied to non-resident counterparties evidenced by offshore-delivery and non-resident-status records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration (Form B13A or G13 EDI acceptance record)
Bill of Lading / airway bill / Cargo Control Document evidencing physical export
Commercial invoice and exchange settlement statements (SWIFT MT103 / DvP settlement advice) evidencing non-resident consideration
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice proving receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess and claw back zero-rated refunds with arrears interest (ETA s 296) and impose a 25% false-statement or gross-negligence penalty on the refund improperly claimed (ETA s 280); ITA s 163(2) imposes a 50% penalty on understated tax; criminal evasion is punishable by fines of up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment (ETA s 327; ITA s 239); the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s 245) and Treaty Article 29(9) principal-purpose limitation apply to artificial ULC look-through structures; directors are jointly and severally liable for collected or unremitted GST/HST (ETA s 323). Although the ETA prescribes no codified 180-day repatriation rule, CRA auditors apply the 180-day benchmark as an evidentiary presumption in export zero-rating and refund audits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority and holds the settlement accounts underlying the Lynx high-value payment system; Canada, however, operates no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration. Exchange controls were fully abolished in 1951, leaving a liberalised regime in which the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) prudentially supervises banks, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) enforces cross-border transactional reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full, unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital accounts; the Canadian dollar is a freely floated G10 currency and no advance central-bank approval is required for dividends, interest, management fees, capital returns, or liquidation proceeds. Profit-remittance hurdles are exclusively fiscal and administrative: a general 25% Part XIII (Income Tax Act) withholding tax on payments to non-residents, treaty-reduced to 5% for dividends paid to a qualifying US corporate parent holding at least 10% of the ULC, and to 0% for arm's-length interest under the Canada-US Treaty, each requiring a completed Form NR301 or W-8BEN-E; CRS/FATCA reporting; and transfer-pricing documentation (Form T106) for non-arm's-length intercompany funding. Alberta imposes no provincial exchange-control overlay, and non-resident ownership of an unlimited liability corporation is expressly permitted. A material nuance is that the ULC remains a Canadian corporation subject to the full Income Tax Act even when a US shareholder elects 'disregarded entity' treatment for US purposes, so the bank's withholding, reporting, and CRS records must cite the ULC's Canadian CRA business number rather than the US EIN alone.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio: a resident exporter, including a proprietary algorithmic high-frequency trading entity earning securities-related income from non-resident counterparties, may retain, invest, and repatriate 100% of export receipts in any currency. The only binding obligations are (i) FINTRAC cross-border EFT reporting for every single incoming or outgoing wire equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000; (ii) FINTRAC large-cash-transaction reporting and the declaration of physical import/export of currency at CAD 10,000; and (iii) Statistics Canada balance-of-payments reporting used exclusively for macroeconomic statistics. For the Alberta ULC, USD-denominated market-making proceeds held in a USD sub-ledger are free balances; the de facto 'surrender discipline' is the entity's internal treasury policy on converting USD to CAD for tax instalments, operating disbursements, and margin calls, not any statutory conversion ratio.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as a supporting disbursement channel, Low as the primary clearing hub. Offshore digital EMIs (UK FCA-authorised, EU PSD2 institutions, and US fintech banks) cannot obtain Lynx or CDSX settlement membership and therefore cannot clear CAD market-making cash legs, margined derivatives, or delivery-versus-payment obligations. As a secondary rail, an overseas EMI may handle small-value vendor, colocation, and director disbursements, but the legal constraints are material: the EMI must either hold FINTRAC money-services-business registration or avoid touching Canadian-source funds; every EFT at or above CAD 10,000 triggers FINTRAC reporting and increases de-risking pressure from the ULC's principal Schedule I bank; and the ULC's AML/ATF programme must contractually oblige the EMI to apply sanctions and PEP screening with audit rights. The core treasury and clearing account must remain at an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical, in-person director/UBO interview is the de facto industry mandate for a first-market ULC account at RBC, TD, BMO, CIBC, and Scotiabank, given the unlimited-liability wrapper, non-resident shareholding, and algorithmic-trading descriptor. Remote or video onboarding is permitted only by banks with mature digital-KYC workflows, notably ATB Financial and exceptionally RBC, and only after submission of a certified passport of every shareholder holding 10% or more of the ULC, a natural-person UBO's Personal Financial Questionnaire (PFQ), and three years of brokerage or custody account statements. In all cases, at least one Alberta-resident director or authorised signatory must attend an in-person interview at a Canadian commercial banking centre bearing original corporate documentation and proof of address; where a US parent appoints officers as authorised signatories, the signing resolutions must be notarised and apostilled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' label is treated by the bank's onboarding engine as a UBO-obscuring or high-liability vehicle, especially when a single US corporate shareholder owns 100% of the shares and no natural person appears in the initial filing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); the ULC's register of directors, officers, and shareholders maintained at the registered office; a signed attestation of significant control by the filing director; a notarised upstream organisational chart identifying every natural person in the chain; an executed unanimous shareholders' agreement if one exists; a sanctions and PEP self-certification for each UBO; and, where unlimited shareholder liability is questioned, a Canadian counsel opinion explaining the mechanics under Alberta law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6499 / NAICS 523130 algorithmic market-making is flagged as a high-velocity money-movement business with no audited track record and with settlement patterns resembling money services business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements, or a certified review engagement plus treasury projections; the relevant dealer or proprietary-trading registration or exemption letters (ASC/IIROC and US FINRA/SEC equivalents); a written AML/ATF compliance programme incorporating FINTRAC transaction-reporting protocols; a pre-clearing broker-dealer letter confirming delivery-versus-payment settlement through CDS and Lynx; and a concise business narrative distinguishing the ULC as a licensed proprietary trader rather than a money-services business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border dependency and thin capitalisation: the US parent is the sole funding party, and the ULC's capital injection may appear as intercompany debt, raising transfer-pricing, substance, and dual-residency concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved capital call resolution and capitalisation table; audited parent financial statements; executed intercompany loan or equity subscription agreements with arm's-length terms; Form T106 where non-arm's-length transactions exceed reporting thresholds; the CRA business number and corporate account verification letters; and a Canadian tax opinion confirming the ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation despite any US check-the-box election.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth opacity: initial and subsequent capital is injected in planned electronic tranches from the parent's brokerage or custody accounts rather than a single operating bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A source-of-funds bundle comprising three years of parent brokerage and custody statements; an institutional bank reference from the remitting institution; the derivative and margin account statements evidencing the source of net capital; a schedule of planned FX conversions; and a treasury policy synchronising the injection cadence with the declared trading calendar to reduce false-positive alerts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late monetary penalty; continued non-filing for three consecutive years may result in a notice of intended administrative strike-off and subsequent dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return with annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance-due date is 3 months after year-end for Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, plus prescribed interest on overdue balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder consent waiving auditor appointment, or appointment of auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Filed in the corporate minute book; not transmitted to a public authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the annual shareholders' meeting, which must be held within 15 months after the previous meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government penalty; if unanimous waiver is not obtained, an independent audit is mandatory for that fiscal year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for a non-offering Alberta ULC if all shareholders unanimously agree each year; audit may be required by an exchange, licensing, or securities-law condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), as elected in accordance with the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta corporate law requires the Register of Members and Register of Directors to be updated continuously. Every share transfer must be recorded with date, consideration, and transferee details. Alberta does not yet require a separate annual UBO declaration to the provincial registry, but beneficial ownership records must be confirmed during the annual corporate records review and updated within 15 days of a change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$12,000–US$35,000 per annum for a medium proprietary trading entity
